transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~41 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Anika Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Ravi Kumar (Solaris CTO), Lena Ortiz (Solaris ML Eng), Markus Jensen (Solaris Infra), Priya Shah (Solaris PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, imperfect):
- Quick review of pilot token/unit economics, caching savings observed, and batching tradeoffs.
- Discussed 8k-sequence KV cache behavior and how it changed tokens-per-dollar for long context workflows.
- Agreed to run one more long-seq benchmark and to produce a short pricing sheet for dedicated burst pool.

Topics: tokens-per-dollar trends, token/sec throughput, caching hit-rate, batching latency vs cost, dedicated vs hosted fallback, next steps + benchmarks

Action items (brief): see action_items field above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. mic check. um we wanted to do a fast pulse on the pilot economics — tokens per dollar, caching wins, batching tradeoffs — and then pick the next benchmark to lock in.
[00:12] Ravi: yeah thanks, Marcus. quick heads up, we've been getting mixed latency at 95th percent — sometimes spikes up to 420 ms which is painful for chat.
[00:22] Anika: noted. I think the spikes line up with cold KV cache misses; the run from last week showed 72% warm hit-rate on short convs but for the long context flows it dropped. we have the logs.
[00:34] Lena: yep, for our doc-analysis flow most sessions go to 6–8k tokens and we see the cache warm up only after a few user turns.
[00:44] Markus: infra note: on the dedicated nodes we saw GPU util jump 18% during batching bursts, but also our observed tokens-per-dollar improved, hmm, by maybe 22%? need to double-check.
[00:56] Marcus: ok good color. quick stat we've been tracking — across the last 48h on the pilot model variant (rwd-opt-13b-int8), we measured approx 11.8k tokens per dollar using default batching and prefix caching for short prompts. but for long-context doc threads the effective tokens/$ fell to ~7.2k when cache misses were frequent. those are ballpark.
[01:14] Priya: can you repeat the units there? tokens per dollar — is that per hour or per run?
[01:18] Marcus: good q, it's aggregate tokens generated per USD for inference compute only, averaged across calls in the window. doesn't include storage or network.
[01:26] Ravi: okay that makes sense.
[01:30] Speaker 1: uh mm, yeah so the big lever then is cache hit-rate and batching window right?
[01:38] Anika: exactly. two levers we looked at — KV prefix caching and dynamic batching. with cache hit-rate higher than 85% we see tokens/$ jump to the 13–15k range because you avoid recompute on prefixes. batching reduces per-token kernel overhead but ups latency for tail calls.
[01:55] Lena: how much latency do we add per batch? we ran a test with batch_size 32 and saw median lat increase like 40 ms.
[02:03] Anika: that matches our numbers — median +30–50 ms at those batch sizes, but p95 can be worse if the queue builds. tradeoff: cost down, tail latency up.
[02:13] Markus: our SLO is 300 ms p95, so if batching pushes us beyond that it's a problem even if tokens/$ looks nice.
[02:20] Marcus: yep that's the classic latency vs cost tension. options: small batching (8–16), micro-batching with strict latency caps, or push high-QPS work to dedicated burst nodes that are provisioned with more GPUs so batching happens more aggressively without queueing.
[02:36] Ravi: quick question — does Redwood provide an autoscale policy that will shift high-load requests to dedicated when latency degrades?
[02:44] Anika: we have smart routing policies; you can tag routes as latency-first or cost-first. the platform can automatically fall back to a compatible variant or higher tier. during the pilot we saw auto-fallback engage once in a region when capacity was constrained.
[02:58] Markus: was that the fallback to a smaller model or different region?
[03:02] Anika: fallback to a compatible model variant with lower memory but similar quality — basically quantized 13b. region fallback only occurs if you opt in for multi-region routing.
[03:12] Lena: can we get the numbers from that fallback event? I want to see p95 and token/unit before and after.
[03:17] Marcus: yes we'll pull those traces. Jordan will share an event CSV.
[03:21] Jordan: I have it, i'll attach. there may be some null fields; the auto-transcription messed with some labels.
[03:26] Ravi: great. 
[03:30] Marcus: oh, and another datapoint — caching savings for our doc summary workload: when we enabled per-session prefix caching we saw an effective compute reduction of about 28% on the backend, which maps roughly to a 26% reduction in compute cost after overhead. but that depends on retention window.
[03:49] Priya: retention window — you mean how long KV stays cached per session?
[03:52] Anika: yes, TTL. in our pilot we used a 30-minute TTL which hits a good sweet spot. 60 minutes increased memory footprint without proportional hit-rate gains.
[04:02] Lena: can TTL be per-route? some flows are multi-hour.
[04:06] Marcus: yes per-route TTL is supported in the config. recommended is shorter for chat and longer for document review flows.
[04:13] Speaker 2: um, what about quantization? you said rwd-opt-13b-int8 — any quality regressions noted?
[04:19] Anika: minimal. we ran our eval set of 400 prompts and saw 0.7% degradation in ROUGE-style metric, subjective checks passed. quantization + caching + batching combo produced best tokens/$ profile.
[04:31] Ravi: good to hear. what's the current tokens/sec number? we've been tracking throughput for latency budgeting.
[04:36] Marcus: on a single dedicated A100-ish node we measured steady-state generation throughput of ~48 tokens/sec for the 13b quantized variant at 512 context; this drops as context grows but batching boosts token/sec for aggregate throughput.
[04:49] Markus: so with batching we can get high aggregate tokens/sec but single-request latency suffers. can we do hybrid: micro-batch for e2e interactive but larger batch for background summarization?
[04:59] Anika: exactly that's the recommended pattern — two route types. interactive route with strict latency caps, lower batching; background route with aggressive batching and longer TTL.
[05:09] Lena: okay that helps. what about cost for dedicated burst pool? we need a price point to compare with cloud-reserved usage.
[05:16] Marcus: Jordan has the pricing draft. short answer: dedicated baseline plus per-GPU-hour for burst usage. with the pilot numbers we expect dedicated + burst to reduce tokens/$ by roughly 15–30% depending on utilization.
[05:29] Jordan: i'll send the sheet right after the call, it shows break-even at ~40% sustained utilization.
[05:36] Ravi: break-even meaning compared to hosted pay-as-you-go?
[05:40] Jordan: yes exactly.
[05:42] Priya: Security quick check — are audit logs and KMS integrations available on the dedicated config?
[05:47] Marcus: yes SOC2-grade audit logs, KMS/HSM support for the private builds. Redwood Private adds customer-managed KMS and you can export logs to your SIEM.
[05:57] Markus: we may need an air-gapped plan for a customer subset, is that in scope?
[06:01] Anika: we have an on-prem package for regulated workloads; that requires longer lead time and entitlements.
[06:07] Ravi: not immediate but flagging. back to econ — can we walk through the plan for the next benchmark?
[06:13] Marcus: sure. proposal: run a long-sequence KV-cache experiment with 8k sequences and three TTL variants (15 min, 30 min, 60 min). measure tokens/$, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, cold vs warm hit cost delta. Anika leads bench, Marcus shares pricing, customer shares production QPS.
[06:31] Lena: timeline?
[06:33] Anika: I can spin up tests tomorrow and share raw CSV by Friday — assuming no infra approvals.
[06:38] Ravi: that fits. we'd like to see cold vs warm cost delta and also a simulated mixed load where 30% of calls are background bulk summarization.
[06:47] Marcus: we'll include that mix. also will run a micro-batching sweep — batch sizes 8, 16, 32 with latency caps and see cost per token.
[06:56] Speaker 3: there's a small transcription hiccup — sometimes names map wrong, sorry.
[07:00] Anika: no worries.
[07:02] Priya: for the micro-batching sweep can you include queue depth histograms? we want to see probability of hitting the latency cap.
[07:09] Marcus: yes queue depth, p99 wait time, and tokens/sec aggregated per minute.
[07:15] Lena: quick nit — earlier you mentioned tokens per dollar numbers that excluded storage and network; for our evaluation we want full TCO including S3 egress because we may store intermediate caches.
[07:26] Jordan: noted, we'll add an addendum showing compute-only vs compute+storage+network.
[07:31] Ravi: oh, and competitor note — one of our infra folks ran a microtest against OpenAI latencies and saw similar median but better p95 at small context sizes; we want to see where Redwood lands for long context.
[07:43] Marcus: understood. Redwood tends to differentiate on long-context economics and on private/dedicated options. we'll aim to show that in the next deck.
[07:51] Markus: any surprises in the pilot logs? errors or memory OOMs?
[07:55] Anika: one OOM during a very large multi-doc query at 32k tokens; that was expected — we throttled that flow afterwards. otherwise stable.
[08:04] Lena: okay.
[08:06] Marcus: quick run of live numbers — i'll read the recent 24h sample: avg tokens per call 2,200; avg tokens generated per USD 10.9k; KV warm hit-rate overall 68%; p95 latency 310 ms across interactive route.
[08:22] Priya: 310 p95 is just above our 300 target. what can we tweak quickly?
[08:27] Anika: small wins: reduce batch size to 12 for interactive, bump dedicated burst capacity for peak hour, and increase TTL for doc review route. all three together pushed p95 under 300 in our sandbox.
[08:40] Ravi: costs for bumping burst capacity — is that an hourly surcharge?
[08:44] Marcus: it's billed as GPU-hour for burst plus small provisioning fee. we'll show examples in the pricing sheet.
[08:51] Lena: can you show a sample daily cost delta for our expected 150k requests/day?
[08:56] Jordan: yes that's a row in the sheet — i will tailor it to 150k/day with mixed route split.
[09:02] Speaker 4: brief pause here while we pull a csv link.
[09:06] Jordan: link pasted in chat — "pilot-bench-11-30.csv" (note there may be header inconsistencies)
[09:11] Marcus: great thanks. any further questions on the numbers?
[09:14] Ravi: question on caching eviction: if we have long-tail users with huge sessions, will KV evict aggressively or do we control LRU?
[09:22] Anika: eviction is LRU-ish, and you can set policy per-route — LRU, TTL-first, or pinned for specific session types. pinned increases memory footprint and can be scoped by user ID.
[09:33] Lena: nice. pinned would help our top 1% power users.
[09:36] Marcus: ok last part — recap and next steps.
[09:40] Marcus: recap: Redwood runs 8k-seq benchmark (Anika), micro-batching sweep (Anika), pricing sheet for dedicated + burst (Marcus/Jordan), include full TCO variant with storage & egress (Jordan), customer to provide QPS and retention requirements (Ravi).
[09:58] Ravi: timeline recap — we aim to have data and pricing in early next week, so we can decide on whether to scale pilot to dedicated.
[10:05] Priya: sounds good. any blockers?
[10:08] Markus: infra approvals to run long-seq test in our staging should be ok, we'll confirm by EOD.
[10:13] Marcus: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll sync asynchronously on the CSV and pricing.
[10:20] Jordan: thanks, attaching the CSV and the sketch pricing in chat now.
[10:25] Lena: thanks all. bye.
[10:27] Ravi: thanks. bye.

End of transcript.
